title: Integral closure commutes with localization (Stacks 0307)
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $S\subseteq A$ be a multiplicative subset, and let $B'\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Let $S^{-1}A$ and $S^{-1}B$ be the localizations [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] (with $S$ acting on $B$ through $\varphi$), and $S^{-1}A\to S^{-1}B$ the induced ring map. Then the map $S^{-1}B'\to S^{-1}B$ induced by the inclusion $B'\subseteq B$ is injective, and its image is the integral closure of $S^{-1}A$ in $S^{-1}B$: an element of $S^{-1}B$ is integral over $S^{-1}A$ if and only if it can be written $b/\varphi(s)$ with $b\in B'$ and $s\in S$.
